title: ESA Week in Images: 5 to 9 October 2026
summary: ESA's weekly photo roundup covered Earth views, deep-space sightings, spacecraft hardware testing and a few people-focused announcements. It offers a quick look at the range of work happening across the agency.

sections.heading: Views of Earth
sections.body: Sentinel-3C imaged Italy and the area beyond it this week. A Copernicus Sentinel-2 image acquired on 5 April 2026 shows Etosha National Park in northern Namibia. Both are satellites in Europe's Earth-observation fleet.

sections.heading: Sightings Across the Solar System
sections.body: Hera sent back its first glimpse of Didymos, its destination. Mars Express captured the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud, and Webb showed commotion from the stellar jets of a nebula, a glowing cloud of gas and dust. Trisat-S also took an image of the Sun.

sections.heading: Hardware Under Test
sections.body: Lunar Pathfinder was shown during its integration and testing campaign at SSTL in the United Kingdom. LandCam-X was pictured as it was integrated onto the Griffin-1 lander, and MPAc went through a vibration test. Engineers also followed a rover's moves in the desert, and images showed the three terminals of ESA's UWB technology demonstrator.

sections.heading: People and New Projects
sections.body: Géraldine Naja was pictured with the WIA-Europe award. ESA and Pi School also presented EVE.
